title: Legazpi's Expedition from Mexico to the Philippines
intro: In 1564 the viceroy of New Spain commissioned Miguel López de Legazpi, by order of Philip II, to lead an expedition across the Pacific to find the Spice Islands. Five ships carried 500 soldiers, over half of them Mexicans, and six Augustinian missionaries, with Andrés de Urdaneta as navigator.
ending: Legazpi proclaimed Manila the capital in 1571 and became the first Spanish governor-general of the Philippines. He died in Manila on 20 August 1572, and the expedition created the trans-Pacific Manila galleon trade.

legs.title: Across the Pacific and through the Visayas

stops.text: Five ships with 500 soldiers sailed from this port in New Spain. Other sources give 1 November 1564 and mention four ships and 379 men.
stops.quote: On 19 or 20 November 1564, five ships, carrying 500 soldiers, over half of whom were Mexicans (Criollos, Mestizos and Indios) and the remaining, Spaniards, sailed from the port of Barra de Navidad, New Spain, in what is now Jalisco state, Mexico

stops.text: After sailing the Pacific for 93 days the expedition anchored briefly in the Mariana Islands and took on supplies. There they fought with Chamorro people and burned several huts.
stops.quote: In 1565, they landed in the Mariana Islands, where they briefly anchored and replenished their supplies. There they fought with Chamorro tribes and burned several huts.

stops.text: Sikatuna, a chief of Bohol, had given Legazpi information about Cebu and joined him as a guide. The ships anchored off the Rajahnate of Cebu but did not land, because people there opposed them.
stops.quote: López de Legazpi's expedition anchored off the Indianized Rajahnate of Cebu on 13 February 1565, but did not put ashore due to opposition from natives.

stops.text: The expedition reached the island of Samar and made a blood compact with its chief, Datu Urrao.
stops.quote: On 22 February 1565, the expedition reached the island of Samar and made a blood compact with its chief, Datu Urrao.

stops.text: From Samar the Spaniards went on to the island of Limasawa, where Datu Bankaw received them.
stops.quote: The Spaniards then proceeded to Limasawa and were received by Datu Bankaw

stops.text: On Bohol the Spaniards befriended Datu Sikatuna and Rajah Sigala. Legazpi made a blood compact with Sikatuna on 16 March.
stops.quote: then to Bohol, where they befriended Datu Sikatuna (or Catunao) and Rajah Sigala. On 16 March 1565, López de Legazpi made a blood compact with Datu Sikatuna.

stops.text: The expedition returned to Cebu and landed. Rajah Tupas challenged the Spaniards but was overpowered, and they founded a colony, the Villa del Santisimo Nombre de Jesús, named after an image of Sto. Niño. In 1568 a Portuguese blockade failed.
stops.quote: On 27 April 1565, the expedition returned to Cebu and landed there. Rajah Tupas challenged the Spaniards, but was overpowered.

stops.text: Food was scarce in Cebu, so Legazpi moved to the town of Panay on the island of Panay. The Spaniards then founded a second settlement, Capiz, on the bank of the Panay River.
stops.quote: In 1569, due to a scarcity of food provisions in Cebu, López de Legazpi transferred to Panay town on the island of Panay.

stops.text: Legazpi sent Martín de Goiti north with 120 Spaniards. Goiti landed in Batangas and on 8 May reached Manila Bay, where he formed an alliance with Rajah Matanda, a vassal of the Sultan of Brunei.
stops.quote: Landing in Batangas with a force of 120 Spaniards, de Goiti explored the Pansipit River, which drains Taal Lake. On 8 May, they arrived in modern Manila Bay.

stops.text: Bambalito's fleet of two thousand five hundred fought the Spaniards under Goiti at Bangkusay Channel and lost, and the Spaniards occupied Tondo and Maynila. Legazpi made a pact with Rajah Sulayman and Lakan Dula, founded a settlement and proclaimed Manila the capital.
stops.quote: López de Legazpi established a settlement there on 24 June 1571, and he also ordered the construction of the walled city of Intramuros. He proclaimed the town Manila to be the island's capital.

stops.text: Legazpi governed the Philippines for a year before he died of a stroke in Manila, bankrupt. He was buried in San Agustin Church, Intramuros.
stops.quote: López de Legazpi governed the Philippines for a year before dying suddenly of a stroke in Manila on 20 August 1572 after scolding an aide.

notes: The article is confused in places: Bangkusay Channel is dated 3 June 1571 but Goiti's landing 8 May is under 1570, and the fleet sailed '30 May 1570'. I used 1570 for the Manila Bay landing (the article's year) and left the battle's date out. 'Mariana Islands' stop: the article names no island; wp set to Guam only to give a point, editor may prefer the archipelago's entry point. Limasawa has no date in the article. Legazpi himself stayed in Cebu while Goiti went to Luzon (the article says he did not accompany the conquest of Maynila and followed 'the following year'); the Manila Bay stop is Goiti's, as the article tells it. Left out: Mindoro, Ilin and Lubang (Salcedo's, no Legazpi), Lubao, Betis, Calumpit, Malolos (Goiti's, passing). The Manila stop of 1571 'by sea' is the article's silence about how Legazpi travelled. Cebu quote: Sikatuna's guiding is from the article's first sentence of the section.
